item.title: Hegseth 'state of the force' speech: US to cut number of generals, admirals by 20%
item.description:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced Wednesday that the United States has slashed the number of its generals and admirals by 20 percent, in a move he said is aimed at "accountability." Hegseth suggested the cuts targeted officers who failed to get on board with his efforts to ensure the military is focused on war-fighting rather than the "woke" policies of previous administrations, describing the reductions as an "accomplishment." FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Philip Turle tells us more.

item.title: White House airs new taxpayer-funded ad praising Trump’s war on Iran
item.description:
From leaked reports showing the U.S. Army preparing potential options around Cuba to the U.S. Navy’s strategic tactical shift away from the Iranian blockade line, Murtaza Hussain and Sarmad Jawad analyze what’s driving these moves—and what Trump’s post-midterm foreign policy strategy could look like. Plus, a look into Iran’s updated terminal guidance missile capabilities, the human toll aboard US naval deployments, and how $100+ oil prices are shaping negotiations over the Strait of Hormuz. Then a deep dive into the rise of China in the Trump era as Xi Jinping pays a state visit for the first time in 10 years. Drop Site News is an independent news outlet covering war and politics. item.title: Iraq’s Kurdish forces look to a new era after US withdrawal
item.description:
More than two decades after the United States invaded Iraq, American forces have completed their withdrawal from the country, marking the end of the Operation Inherent Resolve mission in Iraq. U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) announced Wednesday that American forces and equipment had completed an “orderly departure” from Erbil Air Base in northern Iraq, formally ending the U.S. military mission there. The withdrawal is part of a planned transition toward a bilateral U.S.-Iraq defense relationship. While American forces are no longer stationed in Iraq as part of Operation Inherent Resolve, the Combined Joint Task Force-Operation Inherent Resolve (CJTF-OIR) remains operational and is now headquartered in Jordan. Operation Inherent Resolve was established in 2014 after ISIS seized large swaths of Iraq and Syria, with U.S. and coalition forces working to defeat the terrorist organization.…

Dozens of states, cities, counties and tribes have sued major oil companies . item.title: Portugal coach responds after Ronaldo leaves camp
item.description:
Cristiano Ronaldo has left Portugal’s training camp after several days of tensions with head coach Jorge Jesus. Portuguese Football Federation president Pedro Proença travelled to Copenhagen to try to ease the situation, without success. Ronaldo eventually missed training and left Denmark on his private jet. The five-time Ballon d’Or winner must now explain his decision.

item.title: Africa's richest man launches Kenya oil refinery despite land protests
item.description:
Africa’s richest man Aliko Dangote formally kicked off construction of a $16 billion oil refinery in Kenya on Wednesday, aiming to replicate the success of his plant in Nigeria which has turned the country into a fuel-producing powerhouse amidst a global energy crisis. The new refinery on the island of Lamu is set to be completed in 2030, ultimately refining 700,000 barrels a day. It will serve a region that has historically relied on Middle East fuel imports as part of a broader push to strengthen Africa’s energy security and bolster economic growth. Kenya’s President William Ruto was joined at the groundbreaking ceremony by the presidents of Ethiopia and Uganda. The planned refinery already faces competition from upcoming projects in Tanzania and Uganda, however. item.title: The trouble with Flock cameras is the surveillance system’s architecture, not just some of its users
item.description:
Flock cameras capture a vehicle’s license plate, location and distinguishing marks down to dents or a bumper sticker. Buena Vista Images/Getty Images Wherever Marci Bakely went, her ex-boyfriend seemed to know. When the Georgia single mother drove to the grocery store or a date, he often texted within minutes. According to a Washington Post investigation , Bakely’s ex-boyfriend, Braselton Police Chief Michael Steffman, searched her license plates and those of her teenage daughter roughly 600 times through Flock Safety, a company that makes and operates networks of automated license plate readers, or ALPRs. The Georgia Bureau of Investigation arrested Steffman in November 2025 on charges of stalking, harassment and misuse of an ALPR. He was found dead before trial. Bakely’s case is not unique . item.title: Passengers recount chaos on Tel Aviv flight. And, FBI probes employee-data hack
item.description:
The hackers behind the massive FBI breach told 404 Media on Monday they do not intend to publish the data. The breach, in which the hackers stole personal information on “all FBI employees and applicants” including physical addresses, job roles, names of spouses, and medical records, represents a significant national security and counterintelligence threat. Criminals in the same ecosystem as the hacking group, called ShinyHunters, have previously used hacked phone data to track and harass the FBI agents investigating them. When 404 Media first broke news of the breach, the group sent the personal data of an agent and their spouse who they said was investigating the group.

item.title: The Case for Good Faith
item.description:
I've never been sure how to pronounce it. Bo-nah feed-ays? Bah-nah fieds? The term bona fides trips me up every time. But it's an important concept, so I try my best. You might even say I make…a good faith effort. To argue in good faith—the literal translation of the Latin—means assuming that the person on the other side is saying what he actually believes and that disagreement is not itself evidence of corruption, cowardice, or deceit. And vice versa. The assumption and practice of good faith makes intellectual debate possible. And yet it feels increasingly rare. Tell someone you favor free trade and you will quickly learn you are really serving the interests of multinational corporations. Defend immigration and you are importing voters.
